steps_raw.instruction: FACS Aria II Shut Down
Scope and Applicability: This protocol provides step by step instructions for shutting down the BD FACS Aria II and cleaning it of potentially hazardous materials.
Sheath fluid. (BD Bioscience 342003)
P2, P10, P1000 pipets
1 Liter graduated cylinder
BD Falcon 5 ml polystyrene round bottom tubes
Biohazard disposal container
Safely shutdown and cleaned BD FACS Aria II
FACSDiva Software manual
http://static.bdbiosciences.com/documents/FACSDiva8-QRG-Administrator-Guide.pdf
FACS Aria II User Guide
http://static.bdbiosciences.com/documents/BD_FACSAria_II_User_Guide.pdf
Warning: Personal Protective Equipment () should be used at all times while operating this protocol. If you are unsure what you should be using, see your immediate supervisor.
Methodology/Procedures:
Daily Shutdown Procedure.
Remove nozzle and insert the integrated closed loop nozzle
Clean Flow cell 2 times with MilliQ water
Select Cytometer > Cleaning Modes > Clean Flow Cell.
Install a tube containing approximately 4 ml of MilliQH2O, then click Okay.
Turn off the Cytometer main power ( press big green button on the left side of the Aria).
Exit BD Coherent Connection software.
Exit Cytometer Tera Term Program.
Exit BD FACSDiva software and shut down the computer.
Depressurize the sheath tanks and refill with sheath fluid.
Empty waste in sink (add bleach if it was not already in the waste tank).
Turn off Aerosol Management System and Water Cooler if these were used.
Weekly Shutdown Procedure ( Fluidics Shutdown)
Select Cytometer > Fluidics Shutdown. The following window opens: MAKE SURE THERE IS PLENTY OF 70% ETOH IN THE TANK BEFORE STARTING (FILL TO THE WELD LINE)
Remove the nozzle from the flow cell assembly and click Done.
Insert the integrated closed loop nozzle into the flow cell assembly and click Done.
Disconnect the air line from the sheath tank and connect it to the air port on the ETON shutdown tank.
Disconnect the fluid line from the bottom side of the sheath filter and connect it to the ethanol filter on the ethanol shutdown tank.
When prompted, install a tube containing approximately 4 ml of MilliQH2Oon the loading port, then click Done.
Click Okay when you see a message that the system can be turned off.
Exit BD Coherent Connection software.
Exit Cytometer Tera Term Program..
Exit BD FACSDiva software and shut down the computer.
Depressurize the sheath tanks and refill with sheath fluid.
Empty waste in sink (add bleach if it was not already in the waste tank).
Turn off Aerosol Management System and Water Cooler if these were used.
Load and run a tube of 10% bleach for at least a minute at a flow rate of 11.
Repeat with a tube of DI water.
Repeat step 2 through step12 from the Weekly Shutdown Procedure.
Monthly Aseptic Cleaning Procedure
In order to maintain sterility of the fluidic system on the FACS machines, we conduct an aseptic clean the first workday of every month.
For aseptic clean, run the “Prepare for Aseptic Sort” cleaning module. This takes roughly 1 hour.
Press “Cytometer” on the file menu, then go to “Cleaning Modes”, and last “Prepare for Aseptic Sort”.
Follow wizard instruction to carry out aseptic clean. Also consult BD FACSAria II User’s Guide pages 187-190.
Appendix: Handling biologically hazardous samples
Aerosol Management System (AMS)

Our Aria has an Aerosol Management System that is used to contain all aerosols that arise during the sort process. This consists of a separate vacuum unit that pushes air through a 0.12-µm ultra-low penetration air (ULPA) filter, and a series of drilled holes to allow airflow through the sort chamber and collection area. All doors must be closed for this to work correctly.
If using this system, conduct all sorting setups with it on, since the airflow can affect the side streams.
When sorting human material, or other potentially hazardous samples, the Aerosol Management System (AMS) must be used.
Ensure that the main POWER button on the back of the evacuator is on.
Press the POWER button on the membrane panel of the evacuator.
Ensure that the suction control rate is set to 20%.(Do not set the suction control rate above 20%, higher rates could affect the stability of the side streams.)
Verify that the filter flow gauge reads less than 2.4 inches.
If a clog is encountered, do the following steps:
Turn stream off (keep top and flow chamber doors CLOSED)
Turn up suction rate to 100% and allow at least 1 minute to evacuate aerosols from the sort chamber.

Remove nozzle and conduct appropriate cleaning procedures. Place a nozzle in a clean FACS tube with MilliQH2O, close tube with a cap and sonicare it for 1 min in Sonicator. Take out nozzle from a tube and dry with kimwipes.
Reset suction to 20% and begin stream again.
Put AMS on standby by pressing the POWER button on the membrane panel when you are finished sorting.
